body:
The main issue I see here is that collision point + collision normal offset will be unreliable for a tile polygon corners with angle `<= 90` degrees. For 90 degrees (so including typical square grid) the normal offset would only slide the collision point along the edge, resulting in the same issue as for checking the cell directly at the collision point. For corners with `< 90` degrees (two corners in typical 2:1 isometric grid) the normal offset applied at the corner would overshoot to the neighboring cell.
Simple example scene

```tscn [gd_scene load_steps=6 format=3 uid="uid://c8mhtflbyl42u"] [ext_resource type="Texture2D" uid="uid://darrr6rw5a6gl" path="res://icon.png" id="1_641wp"] [sub_resource type="TileSetAtlasSource" id="TileSetAtlasSource_7082j"] texture = ExtResource("1_641wp") texture_region_size = Vector2i(64, 64) 0:0/0 = 0 0:0/0/physics_layer_0/polygon_0/points = PackedVector2Array(-32, -32, 32, -32, 32, 32, -32, 32) [sub_resource type="TileSet" id="TileSet_1jc5k"] tile_size = Vector2i(64, 64) physics_layer_0/collision_layer = 1 sources/0 = SubResource("TileSetAtlasSource_7082j") [sub_resource type="GDScript" id="GDScript_l5aku"] script/source = "extends TileMapLayer func collision_to_map_point_only(collision_point: Vector2, collision_normal: Vector2) -> Vector2i: return local_to_map(to_local(collision_point)) func local_to_map_normal_offset_local(collision_point: Vector2, collision_normal: Vector2) -> Vector2i: var global_inv: Transform2D = global_transform.affine_inverse(); return local_to_map((global_inv * collision_point) - 0.5 * global_inv.basis_xform(collision_normal).normalized()) func local_to_map_normal_offset_global(collision_point: Vector2, collision_normal: Vector2) -> Vector2i: return local_to_map(to_local(collision_point - collision_normal)) func get_cell_local_rect(coords: Vector2i) -> Rect2: return Rect2(coords * tile_set.tile_size, tile_set.tile_size) " [sub_resource type="GDScript" id="GDScript_w68wu"] script/source = "extends RayCast2D @onready var tm: TileMapLayer = owner @onready var target_tm_local_rect: Rect2 = tm.get_cell_local_rect(tm.get_used_cells()[0]) func _process(delta: float) -> void: global_position = get_global_mouse_position() var target_tm_local = tm.to_local(global_position).max(target_tm_local_rect.position).min(target_tm_local_rect.end) target_position = (global_transform.affine_inverse() * tm.global_transform) * target_tm_local target_position += 32 * target_position.normalized() queue_redraw() func _draw() -> void: if not is_colliding(): return var cell_coords: Vector2i #cell_coords = tm.collision_to_map_point_only(get_collision_point(), get_collision_normal()) #cell_coords = tm.local_to_map_normal_offset_global(get_collision_point(), get_collision_normal()) cell_coords = tm.local_to_map_normal_offset_local(get_collision_point(), get_collision_normal()) draw_set_transform_matrix(global_transform.affine_inverse() * tm.global_transform) draw_rect(tm.get_cell_local_rect(cell_coords), Color(Color.GREEN_YELLOW, 0.3)) draw_line(tm.to_local(get_collision_point()), tm.to_local(get_collision_point() + 32 * get_collision_normal()), Color.BLUE) " [node name="TileMapLayer" type="TileMapLayer"] tile_map_data = PackedByteArray(0, 0, 5, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) tile_set = SubResource("TileSet_1jc5k") script = SubResource("GDScript_l5aku") [node name="RayCast2D" type="RayCast2D" parent="."] script = SubResource("GDScript_w68wu") ```

| Cell at collision point | Cell at collision point - normal offset | |--------|--------| ![mNRIRKVmgn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b4f47c8-77ec-4186-975f-7e1411fec0b5)|![jsmUQcleha](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab58e528-9710-4923-a7a7-de446444e511) --- Besides, this method assumes that the collision polygon doesn't exceed the tile's area, this would need to be mentioned. Also a collision polygon might be e.g. only a thin strip on the inner side of an edge, in such case normal offset could lead to overshooting to the neighbor cell as well (but that's an actual edge case :upside_down_face:).
tbh I opened this PR thinking it's going to be simple to implement. I don't feel like resolving these issues :/
